speaker: valeriemorris
text: Okay, the topics discussed was it was at 9.30 in the morning till 11. And the topics were recovery, resiliency, and reinventing sport and recreation in rural communities. Beckwith-Reeve Richard Kidd did the introductions, welcomed everybody and thanked them for their attendance. He welcomed the keynote speakers, which were Kevin Lee from Algonquin College and Jason Jansen, Executive Director from Ontario Basketball. He reported mostly on the reported revenue losses. Losses, he quoted 1.7 million lost. However, they were able to recover and receive funds from canceled Ontario basketball events of 1.3 million. And as of March the 11th, 2020, all NBA championships cups canceled. They anticipate the summer of 2021 to return to outdoor basketball. And the panelists that were involved in the questions and answers were Emily Wimpenny from Brockville Y, Kelly McGann from the Frontenac Arch Biosphere Fab Nature Camp, Scott Rice from Westport Rideau Lakes Storm Softball Team, and Ryan Carroll, Carleton Place Minor Girls Hockey League. And open questions and answers took place with most of the questions and answers, concentrating and emphasizing on how damaging to the students being unable to participate in outdoor games and activities, both to their physical and their mental health and the need to recover and to return to outdoor organized sports of all kinds is imperative. The main purpose of the Rural Recreation Association Executive Committee is to develop the structure for a non-profit recreation and physical activity association that serves Lanark, Leeds and Grenville and the surrounding region. The association will work to facilitate planning, professional development, communications, and the sharing of resources between individuals and organizations involved in physical activity and recreation. The executive committee is also responsible for planning the annual recreation summit and the AGM, which usually takes place at the Smith Falls Community Center. And of course, in the summer of 2020 was canceled due to COVID-19. However, this year's planning stages, it's in the planning stages, be it live or virtual, that's dependent on how everyone behaves and how COVID is at the moment. The Rural Roundtable is also open to new and existing members and they encourage people to join. The annual elections take place November and it's a two-year member commitment. They are looking for more members. The next virtual event webinar for the RRA is in the works and a date will be advised shortly. So they are looking for suggestions for topics to discuss and guest speakers, if anybody has any ideas which they'd like to submit. Cassandra McGregor from Beckwith Township is the contact. That's it.
